summary: Plausible; duplicates nothing landed, running or do-not-retry. Two spec errors to fix before the build: residual coefficients are per-channel [8192] vectors, not scalars, and post_ffn applies (1+w) as an input scale before the RMS. The T=9..32 full-width unpooler will probably be flat or slower than nvjet, so decode_16/32 'faster' rests almost entirely on the boundaries.
justification: At T<=8 the replaced chain (nvjet sliced unpooler 8.4 MB + splitKreduce + F.pad, ~9 us vs a ~3 us P-body GEMV) is real overhead; the P-body GEMV already runs fault-free at ~3.4-3.6 TB/s for NF=1. Fusing both boundaries with an immediate launch_dependents makes attn boundary -> P the first adjacent hand-written pair, so P's W_pr prefetch overlaps for real: decode_1/verify_1 ~5-8 us. Incumbents are stale (master decode_1 127.5/142.9). Weakest link: the T=9..32 full-width unpooler (NF=2/4) inherits P's x L2 re-read (2.85 TB/s at T=32, ~3.1 at T=16) vs master nvjet ~3.1-3.2 TB/s: parity at T=16, up to ~2 us slower at T=32. At T=1 the one-CTA boundary runs two dependent block reductions over ~100 KB, ~2-3 us vs SGLang 3.6. Spec errors: (1) alpha = sqrt(clamp(sigmoid(-w/0.3)*(1+sigmoid(w/0.3)), 1e-3)) and beta = sigmoid(w/0.3) per channel; attn/ffn_residual_gate are [8192] (reference.py:109,123,339-344), so alpha/beta must be fp32 [8192] device vectors from the module's precomputed buffers, not scalars, else dlb_ok goes False and the check measures master. (2) ffn boundary (reference.py:472-476): stream2 = alpha2*stream1 + beta2*rms(f*(1+post_ffn_norm), 1e-8); (1+w) is an INPUT scale before the RMS; only the attn post-norm has no weight; next attention input rms(stream2)*(1+next_pre_attn_norm) eps 1e-5. (3) Optional: at T<=8, f columns 1024..8191 are zero, so the ffn boundary can read 1024 columns. Headline ~+1.5-2.5%, inside CI; read profile rows.
confounders: small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (base): overlap exists only because P is PDL-launched; re-run _dl_self_check graph (attn_boundary -> P -> R -> experts) with the new boundary; part of any gain shows as a shorter P row.
post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: the unpooler's predecessor (Triton at T<32, SGLang at T=32); self-check must cover both layouts through the real _experts.
stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1: no interaction at T<=32; stale incumbents only.
interference: No companion. Rows dl_boundary_kernel, dl_unpool_kernel<1> (T<=8) and dl_unpool_kernel<2/4> (T=9..32) are separable from master's rows; a shorter P row isolates the PDL overlap; verify_16/32 are the drift control. Build note: in prepare time dl_unpool_kernel vs _gemm per NF on synthetic data and keep nvjet for any NF where the custom kernel is slower; print the pick per NF. Overlaps: dense-chain-stage2 (kernel-disjoint, same TU: textual conflict, complementary); split-KV checks (no overlap); dl-route-warp-topk-pdl edits P and R in the same TU; dl-p-wide-tile-t16-t32 fixes the x re-read this inherits.
rules_flags: No rules problems: alpha/beta and norm weights from prepare weights; self-resetting fixed-order ticket split-K; every global write and activation read after griddepcontrol.wait; timing only in prepare.
Keep zero stores to ffn_output columns 1024..8191 after griddepcontrol.wait.
Only judge-proven instruction forms, -lineinfo, sync+print after each new kernel in the self-check, okc check first.
open_questions: dl_boundary_kernel CUDA-event time at T=1 with one CTA vs SGLang 3.6/3.7 us? If >= 3 us, several CTAs per token?
Does SGLang FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm read alpha/beta as precomputed fp32 buffers or recompute from bf16 gates? Match its rounding.
Is dl_unpool_kernel<2/4> faster than nvjet at T=9..32 in prepare timing? If not, gate it off.
